purpose: Probe-by-probe classification of the production-like readiness harness execution requested for the current release review. Every PASS is tied to an actually executed test with a run identifier. Preflight, static, mocked and bounded evidence is classified separately and is never counted as execution evidence.

classification_vocabulary.PASS (EXECUTED): An actual test ran against real services/runtime and its result is recorded in immutable evidence.
classification_vocabulary.PASS (EXECUTED) / SCOPED: Executed, but the harness itself states a scope limit; the limit is reproduced verbatim.
classification_vocabulary.PARTIAL: Some sub-probes genuinely executed and passed; other named sub-probes did not execute and stay BLOCKED.
classification_vocabulary.BLOCKED: Required sub-probe was not executed anywhere; no claim is made.
classification_vocabulary.ENVIRONMENT-BLOCKED: The requested host/runner cannot provide the capability; recorded instead of simulated.
classification_vocabulary.PASS / BOUNDED: Real local harness execution with synthetic filesystem-shaped fixtures; explicitly not production evidence.
classification_vocabulary.FAIL (EXECUTED): An actual test ran and genuinely failed. Recorded as a defect, never reclassified.

encryption_key_defect_closure.root_cause: Frappe writes encryption_key into sites/<site>/site_config.json lazily, on the first call to frappe.utils.password.get_encryption_key(); bench new-site does not create it. foundation.localhost installs only erpnext/education/payments/hrms, so nothing triggered key generation before the first backup. The harness then copied the key with `if "encryption_key" in original_config:` - a silent no-op - and reported the omission as a passive observation instead of failing the run. placement-test.localhost installs toefl_house, whose after_install() calls get_encryption_key(), which is why that path reported true and masked the defect.

stricter_probe_rerun.evidence_quality_defect_found_by_this_ru: innodb_recovery_messages contained exactly one line, '[Entrypoint]: Starting temporary server'. That is container startup noise, not InnoDB crash recovery, so the non-empty check was satisfied while the label overstated the evidence. Commit e92c66e separates crash markers from startup markers, records SHOW ENGINE INNODB STATUS's LOG section as the authoritative native source, and requires innodb_force_recovery=0 so recovery cannot be silently bypassed.
stricter_probe_rerun.note: The substantive durability proof was never affected: identical CRC32 checksum, identical row count, rolled-back uncommitted transaction and enforced binlog rotation were all present. The defect was in how one corroborating field was labelled, and it is recorded here rather than quietly corrected.

honest_labelling_rerun.why_this_run_is_the_authoritative_durabi: It is the first run in which the crash scenario is corroborated by an authoritative native source rather than a log grep. innodb_recovery_messages is correctly EMPTY - MariaDB 11.8 emits no crash-recovery lines at default verbosity - and the previously mislabeled startup noise now sits in its own server_startup_messages field. SHOW ENGINE INNODB STATUS supplies the real recovery position (log sequence number 52305 equal to log flushed up to 52305, last checkpoint at 51911), and innodb_force_recovery=0 proves recovery was not bypassed. The run would now fail closed if neither a genuine InnoDB log line nor an INNODB STATUS LOG section were present.

independent_recovery_execution.claim_being_tested: P3 - restore onto a genuinely independent execution environment or system, NOT the same host, under an explicit destructive scenario, proving database recovery, private and public file recovery, and application usability afterwards.

hostname.note: The platform reuses generated hostnames across separate ephemeral VMs, observed in run 35143620884, so a hostname is recorded as an observation and never as proof of separation or of sameness.

docker_daemon_id.note: The runner image ships a pre-generated daemon key, so separate VMs from the same image report the same id; observed in run 35168111875. Recorded as an observation only.

destructive_scenario.interpretation: A real destructive trigger ran before any transfer: the database was dropped and the site directory plus both files were removed, with drop-site explicitly told not to archive. Nothing survived on the source to fall back on, so everything the target recovered came from the transferred backup alone.

encryption_key_not_supplied_to_restore.reason: Plaintext key material must not travel through an artifact, so the recovered site runs under its own generated key and fields the source encrypted stay intact but undecryptable here.

admin_credential_is_the_targets_own.reason: The backup carries the source's password hash but not its plaintext, so the recovering system establishes its own credential.

secret_hygiene.statement: The site config backup that frappe writes beside the dumps - which holds the database password and the site encryption key - is excluded from staging by an explicit allowlist, the staged text is scanned for every generated secret, `bench restore --encryption-key` is deliberately unused, and the recovering system sets its own Administrator credential with native `bench set-admin-password`. No plaintext secret travels in any artifact or appears in this ledger; only SHA-256 fingerprints are recorded.

usability_after_recovery.note: Usability is proven over real HTTP through an nginx front proxy in front of Gunicorn, configured as the pinned bench template configures production, and the login is a real session cookie held by the same client used for every later read. The privacy boundary is exercised from both sides: the private file is refused anonymously and served to the session, the public file is served anonymously by nginx from the recovered public directory.

encrypted_field_limitation_asserted.conclusion: Database and files recovered; source-encrypted field is intact but undecryptable here because the key was never transferred. Closing this requires separately controlled external key custody, which is a distinct requirement.
encrypted_field_limitation_asserted.classification: EXPECTED FAILURE, asserted rather than hidden - this is the executed evidence that external key custody (P4) is a distinct outstanding requirement

additional_scope_limits: Both halves are GitHub-hosted runners from the same pool: kernel_boot_id, runner_name and dmi_product_uuid prove separate ephemeral VMs, not separate providers, regions or datacentres. Loss of a host, region or provider remains unexercised.
The backup moves through a GitHub Actions artifact between two ephemeral VMs. There is no off-site or air-gapped destination, no versioned encrypted backup set, no retention policy and no rotation.
Session revocation on recovery, which D8-BACKUP-RECOVERY also requires, is not exercised.
No RPO or RTO is measured against an owner-selected objective, because no owner objective exists and none is invented. Step timings are in the check logs but are not a qualification.
Every record, file and credential is synthetic and generated inside the run; no production workload is exercised.

defects_found_and_fixed_by_execution.detail: The independence verdict compared only runner_name and hostname and treated a Docker daemon id as corroborating. Both halves reported hostname runnervmlun5p, so a genuinely independent pair failed closed on a recycled image name.

After demoting hostname to an observation, /sys/class/dmi/id/product_uuid proved unreadable for the non-root runner user, so the corroborating discriminator had no value and the verdict failed closed on a missing identifier. The reader now falls back across the DMI and firmware paths and reports availability explicitly instead of silently degrading.

GitHub-hosted runners genuinely reuse hostnames across separate VMs: both halves reported runnervmlun5p while kernel_boot_id and runner_name differed. Hostname is not a valid discriminator and is now recorded as an observation annotated with this run.

Both halves also reported the same Docker daemon id because the runner image ships a pre-generated /etc/docker/key.json rather than generating one per boot. Daemon id is likewise demoted to an annotated observation; /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id and the Actions runner name are required to differ, with dmi_product_uuid corroborating when readable.

Login returned HTTP 401 although every other read succeeded. Root cause at pinned frappe 988e54f3: the _new_site restore path calls install_app(force=False, set_as_patched=not source_sql), so with a source SQL file after_install never runs and the --admin-password stashed in frappe.conf is never applied to Administrator. `bench --site <site> set-admin-password` was added after migrate, and the recovering system now sets its own credential so recovery never depends on a source secret.

Login, ping and record reads then all passed, but the private file download returned HTTP 500. Root cause: frappe.utils.response.send_private_file answers an X-Use-X-Accel-Redirect request with the header X-Accel-Redirect: /protected/private/files/<name> and no body, and the generated nginx config had no /protected/ location, so nginx could not resolve the internal offload. Fixed in commit 1378ce4 by declaring the internal /protected/ location the pinned bench template declares, ahead of the /files/ rules so the earlier regex cannot win, and pinned by contract tests.
